plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio leverage and risk.
The remaining book will favor income and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It aims for low drawdown by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: Reduce leveraged ETF exposure across SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, and SPAL to small allocations.
Trim QQQI to 20% to comply with the single-name concentration mandate.
Introduce AAPU with a 4% allocation, leveraging a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure to quality tech and broad indices. Expect moderate volatility and potential for steady growth.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to lean into growth.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Buy AAPU with a 6% allocation, focusing on a high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to stretch for higher growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown risk, daily leverage decay, and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly honored.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero for income focus.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to prioritize monthly distributions.
This plan aims to park cash for yield, reducing high-beta single names.
The portfolio will focus on income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It cuts leverage and high-beta names to near zero, focusing on income ETFs. While aiming for low drawdown, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
